title: Smooth projective completions of curve normalizations after inseparable extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a separated finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $\dim X\leq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There are a finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], a finite set $I$, finite separable extensions $k_i/k'$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and a diagram over $k'$ $$\coprod_{i\in I}Y_i\xrightarrow{\nu}X_{k'},\qquad Y_i\xrightarrow{j_i}\overline Y_i\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(k_i).$$ Here $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $\nu$ is the normalization: explicitly the disjoint union of the normalizations of the reduced irreducible components of $(X_{k'})_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-normalization] [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each $j_i$ is an open immersion with dense nonempty image [def-weil-open-immersion]. Each $\overline Y_i$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], projective [def-kun-projective], and geometrically irreducible over $k_i$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], with dimension at most one. All the schemes displayed are of finite presentation over $k'$. The set $I$ is empty precisely when $X$ is empty.

proof.text: Apply the projective geometrically normal core construction to X. Base change the completion and its dense open immersion along the finite purely inseparable extension. Projectivity survives base change. The projections are homeomorphisms, so the dimension bound survives and the base-changed open immersion still has dense image.

Apply the finite-component geometric-normality theorem. Each projective normalized component is integral, nonempty, of dimension at most one, and geometrically normal. The number of components vanishes exactly when the base-changed completion is empty.

Refine each projective normalized component to its finite separable constant field. The refined structure map is smooth, projective and geometrically irreducible, with the canonical structure-map factorization.

Restrict the components to the base-changed original dense open and normalize them. The component supports are closed, distinct, and enumerate the irreducible components of the base-changed original scheme. Their normalizations form dense nonempty opens in the chosen smooth projective components, compatibly with normalization maps.

Define Y_i as the normalization of the restricted component and B_i as that of the projective component, with identity normalization isomorphism e_i. Define p_i by composing the open immersion with the projective structure map. Define ν as the coproduct of the component normalization maps. The restriction comparison equation and the pullback projection equation give the first commutativity identity, and the constant-field factorization gives the second.

Over a field, the projective components are locally Noetherian and compact, hence Noetherian. Their open subschemes are Noetherian by topological embeddings. Mathlib finite-presentation and Noetherian-space instances therefore give local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of p_i. Local finite presentation passes to the coproduct by source locality; its source is compact as a finite union of compact component images, and is locally Noetherian by local finite type over the field, giving quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. For the projective refined maps, finite field maps and original base-change projection, the same properties follow from properness, finiteness, composition and base change over the Noetherian field. These are direct Mathlib instances, not uses of the previously imported statement-only Noetherian lemmas.
If n=0, the projective base change is empty, and surjectivity of X_K→X and the map X_K→T_K force X empty. Conversely, if X is empty, density of X→T forces T empty, hence T_K empty and n=0.
